title: So too, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, in accordance with Dhamma, the Dhamma-King, relying on Dhamma, honoring Dhamma, respecting Dhamma, venerating…
content: So too, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, in accordance with Dhamma, the Dhamma-King, relying on Dhamma, honoring Dhamma, respecting Dhamma, venerating Dhamma, having Dhamma as his banner, having Dhamma as his flag, having Dhamma as his supremacy, gives protection, shelter, and support in accordance with Dhamma regarding bodily action, thinking: 'Such bodily action should be practiced, such bodily action should not be practiced.' Furthermore, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata... gives protection, shelter, and support in accordance with Dhamma regarding verbal action, thinking: 'Such verbal action should be practiced, such verbal action should not be practiced'; regarding mental action, thinking: 'Such mental action should be practiced, such mental action should not be practiced.' That Tathāgata... having given protection, shelter, and support... regarding bodily action, verbal action, mental action, sets in motion the wheel of Dhamma. That wheel is not to be turned back by any ascetic, brahmin, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone in the world.

title: 'The world, the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is there the world or the concept of the world?" - "Where,…
content: 'The world, the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is there the world or the concept of the world?" - "Where, Samiddhi, there is the eye, there are forms, there is eye-consciousness, there are things cognizable by the eye — there the world or the concept of the world exists. ... Where there is the mind, there are mind-objects, there is mind-consciousness, there are things cognizable by the mind — there the world or the concept of the world exists. And where, Samiddhi, there is no eye, no forms, no eye-consciousness, no things cognizable by the eye — there the world or the concept of the world does not exist. ... Where there is no mind, no mind-objects, no mind-consciousness, no things cognizable by the mind — there the world or the concept of the world does not exist.

title: Furthermore, wanderers, the brahmin says thus: 'I am not anyone's, not anything's anywhere, nor am I anything anywhere. There is nothing belonging to me anywhere,…
content: Furthermore, wanderers, the brahmin says thus: 'I am not anyone's, not anything's anywhere, nor am I anything anywhere. There is nothing belonging to me anywhere, in any way.' The brahmin who says this speaks the truth, not falsehood. Therefore, he does not think of 'ascetic,' does not think of 'brahmin,' does not think 'I am superior,' does not think 'I am equal,' does not think 'I am inferior.' Furthermore, by directly knowing the truth contained therein, he practices the path of nothingness.

title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple reflects: 'Present sensual pleasures and future sensual pleasures, present perceptions of sensual pleasure and future perceptions of sensual pleasure, present…
content: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple reflects: 'Present sensual pleasures and future sensual pleasures, present perceptions of sensual pleasure and future perceptions of sensual pleasure, present forms and future forms, present perceptions of form and future perceptions of form, both are impermanent. What is impermanent is not fit to be delighted in, not fit to be welcomed, not fit to be clung to.' While he practices thus, abides thus often, his mind becomes calm in that element. With a calm mind, he either attains the imperturbable here and now, or he is strongly inclined towards wisdom. With the breakup of the body after death, this situation occurs: that evolving consciousness may, following this, attain the imperturbable.

title: Sorrow, lamentation, and suffering, Various kinds exist in the world. They arise dependent on attachment; Without attachment, they do not arise. Therefore, those who are…
content:
Sorrow, lamentation, and suffering,
Various kinds exist in the world.
They arise dependent on attachment;
Without attachment, they do not arise.
Therefore, those who are happy,

Without sorrow in the world,
Are those who have no attachments.
Therefore, whoever wishes
To be without sorrow, without attachment,
Should not form attachment
To anyone in the world.

title: Samaṇa Gotama abstains from taking what is not given, avoids taking what is not given, takes only what is given, desires only what is given,…
content: Samaṇa Gotama abstains from taking what is not given, avoids taking what is not given, takes only what is given, desires only what is given, lives purely without theft. — Bhikkhus, these are the praises of the Tathāgata by ordinary people. Samaṇa Gotama abstains from sexual misconduct, leads the holy life, lives detached, abstains from base sensual desires. Bhikkhus, these are the praises of the Tathāgata by ordinary people.

title: Brahmin, wisdom is purified by virtue, virtue is purified by wisdom. Where there is virtue, there is wisdom; where there is wisdom, there is virtue.…
content: Brahmin, wisdom is purified by virtue, virtue is purified by wisdom. Where there is virtue, there is wisdom; where there is wisdom, there is virtue. One with virtue certainly has wisdom; one with wisdom certainly has virtue. Virtue and wisdom are considered supreme in the world.

title: Elder Nun Sañjā: Leaving home, going forth, I abandoned my children, Abandoned precious livestock, Abandoned greed and hatred, And regarding ignorance, I live in seclusion.…
content:
Elder Nun Sañjā:

Leaving home, going forth,
I abandoned my children,
Abandoned precious livestock,
Abandoned greed and hatred,
And regarding ignorance,
I live in seclusion.
Having conquered
The root of craving itself,
I live cooled,
Peaceful and calm.

title: ( Blessed One ) One who gives with faith, With a pure mind, Enjoys that food In this life and the next. Therefore, avoid stinginess,…
content:
( Blessed One )
One who gives with faith,
With a pure mind,
Enjoys that food
In this life and the next.
Therefore, avoid stinginess,
Give, remove the stain,
Beings still enjoy
Merit in the next life.

title: Bhikkhus, as long as the bhikkhus do not delight in sleeping, then the bhikkhus will prosper and not decline.
content: Bhikkhus, as long as the bhikkhus do not delight in sleeping, then the bhikkhus will prosper and not decline.
